reproduction_target: Reproduce the computational half of the CHD non-coding variant evaluation: (i) SNP Bind-n-Seq analysis of >3,000 CHD-associated variants for NKX2-5, GATA4 and TBX5 — FASTQ preprocessing/UMI-anchored SNP-window counting, quality thresholding, bound-vs-unbound enrichment, Poisson maximum-likelihood fitting of the concentration-independent association parameter K (scipy.optimize L-BFGS-B, iterative denominator refinement), MEME motif discovery and SNP-position motif-disruption analysis, and the MinSeqChIP / MEME / LS-GKM cross-training model comparison against cardiac TF ChIP-seq (SRX9284027, SRX9284038, SRX2023721) — using the authors' PrOBEX pipeline (github.com/Shreya-droid/SNPoiss_bind_n_seq, pip ProBEX-snp==0.1.2) with the Zenodo datasets named in the repo README; and (ii) the MPRA analysis of 29,048 oligos — barcode/oligo association (MPRAmatch), oligo counting (MPRAcount), DESeq2 activity and allelic-skew calling (MPRAmodel), plotting (mpraprofiler), HOMER v5.1 motif enrichment, and RELI functional-genomics enrichment on emAlleles. Wet-lab generation (protein purification, EMSA-based Bind-n-Seq, Flp-In 293 line construction, MPRA library cloning/transfection/sequencing) is out of computational scope and enters only as W steps.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the Materials and Methods prose of the bioRxiv JATS XML (v1 source.xml; v2 landing page returned 403/429 to WebFetch, v1 XML fetched successfully by curl and is the same manuscript), plus the four repository landing pages and the PrOBEX README prose. No workflow source, notebook, setup.py, or conda-recipe/meta.yaml content was read line-by-line — those are stage-2 objects. The paper carries no numbered 'Code availability' pins beyond PLINK(v1.90b) and HOMER (v5.1); the pip pin ProBEX-snp==0.1.2 and the conda-recipe directory are README-level claims only. Data axis is scored against what the paper states plus what the linked repo README states (the paper's own Data-and-code-availability section names code repositories only; the Zenodo datasets appear in the README, not in the manuscript).

steps.label: SNP Bind-n-Seq variant selection and oligo design: download of 121 CHD-associated SNPs from six GWAS studies via the GWAS Catalog, LD expansion in EUR/AFR/EAS/SAS at R2=0.80 with the TOP LD web tool, removal of indels/incomplete entries, allele permutation, retrieval of 40 bp hg38 flanks, adapter+UMI addition, yielding 13,039 oligos

MPRA variant selection: 157 CHD-associated SNPs from nine GWAS expanded for LD (R2>0.8) on 1000 Genomes ancestry-matched panels using PLINK(v1.90b), variant harmonization to the dbSNP 155 table from the UCSC table browser, 170 bp hg38 flank retrieval plus forward/reverse-complement design, yielding 29,048 oligos

SNP Bind-n-Seq preprocessing: Read 1 of PE150 Illumina data anchored on the constant right flank 'GATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCAC', extraction of the 44 bp SNP-containing window (40 bp genomic + 2x4 bp UMI), per-nucleotide counting at the central SNP position for NKX2-5/GATA4/TBX5 (PrOBEX preprocess_snp_seq.py)

Quality thresholding and enrichment computation: PPM normalization, five stated filters (0nM unbound-to-library ratio outside 0.2-2 excluded; <5 per million in 0nM unbound in both replicates; <5 per million in library; 0nM bound-to-unbound ratio outside 0.2-5; <5 per million across all four bases), pseudo-count (2.5 x total reads)/1e6, bound/unbound enrichment ratios (PrOBEX primary_thresholds.py, secondary_thresholds.py, get_enrichment_calc_*)

Poisson maximum-likelihood binding-affinity model: joint inference of the concentration-independent association parameter K plus the 'stuck-in-the-well' parameter over library/bound/unbound counts for both replicates, denominators initialized at 0.9/max-enrichment and iterated (Poisson model without the extra parameter up to 1000 iterations, denominators taken at iteration 361), 10 iterations of L-BFGS-B via scipy.optimize.minimize, TBX5 500 nM excluded (PrOBEX get_thedenominators_iteratively.py, fitting_poisson_eQ_2_also_withUnb_with_bi.py)

MEME motif discovery: whole-dataset MEME run across all three TFs for motif QC, then per-TF MEME on the top 500 sequences by enrichment with -meme-mod anr, -minw 5, -maxw 9, -meme-nmotifs 5 (PrOBEX run_MEME_ChIP_v1.py; README states the MEME Suite must be separately downloaded into the working directory, with no version)

Motif analysis by SNP position: top-500 K-fitted sequences into MEME 'anr' mode with width 5-6 for NKX2-5 and up to 10 logos on both strands, selection of the highest-scoring PWM, UMI trimming, 40-nt reference/alternate windows plus reverse complements, PWM scoring and highest-scoring subregion identification, SNP-overlap frequency bar plots and binned contribution plots for GATA4/TBX5/NKX2-5 (PrOBEX SNPscore_memePWM_logo_with_bars.py, motif_affected_unaffected_bySNP.py)

Model training and testing / cross-dataset generalization: top-500 SNPs by K split 300 train / 200 test, cardiac TF ChIP-seq SRX9284027 (NKX2.5), SRX9284038 (GATA4), SRX2023721 (TBX5) top-1000 peak-signal sequences split into train/test, four train/test cases, negatives from LS-GKM getNullSeqs, evaluated with MinSeqChIP (min monomer 2, max monomer 6, max gap 1, order-5 non-gapped Markov model, PWM cutoff 40), MEME (same parameters) and LS-GKM (default mode)
MPRA barcode-to-oligo association with the MPRAmatch pipeline on NovaSeq X Plus 2x150 bp data at ~30X coverage (paper cites https://github.com/tewhey-lab/MPRAmatch)

MPRA oligo counting with the MPRAcount pipeline (https://github.com/tewhey-lab/MPRA_oligo_barcode_pipeline) on NextSeq 2000 P3 100-cycle cDNA/plasmid libraries (~100M reads per sample, five replicates); oligos retained if supported by at least 10 barcodes

MPRA activity and allelic-skew calling: DESeq2 median-of-ratios depth normalization, DESeq2 Wald test for plasmid-DNA vs cDNA fold change with Bonferroni correction (regulatory effect at adjusted p<0.01), allelic skew by Wald test on reference vs alternate log ratios with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment at 5% FDR (https://github.com/tewhey-lab/MPRAmodel)
MPRA plotting and visualization with mpraprofiler (https://github.com/WeirauchLab/mpraprofiler)

HOMER (v5.1) motif enrichment on 50 bp reference and alternate FASTA centered on the CVD-associated SNP using findMotif.pl with a background generated by the homer2 background function, removal of motifs shared between reference and alternate alleles, unique SNP-TF/family pair counting, plus HOMER enrichment of emAllele vs non-emAllele sequences

RELI functional-genomics dataset enrichment: intersection of emAllele coordinates with a large internal ChIP-seq/histone-mark collection, significance against a negative set of variants with no CRE activity (50% expression fold change), run for all emAlleles and for the cardiac-CRE-overlapping subset (https://github.com/WeirauchLab/RELI)

Recombinant TF domain expression and purification: NKX2-5 homeodomain (Asp16-Leu96) in pET-51(+) with Strep-Tag II and C-terminal 10xHis, TBX5 T-box domain (Met51-Ser248) in a 6xHis pET vector, GATA4 DBD/ZF (Uniprot P43694, Met207-Ala333) in pET-28a(+); Ni-NTA affinity chromatography

SNP Bind-n-Seq wet protocol: oligopool touchdown PCR amplification, TF binding reactions at 0/100/500/1000/1500/2000/3000 nM, EMSA on 6% polyacrylamide, IR700 imaging, bound/unbound band excision, streptavidin bead purification, barcoding PCR and Illumina PE150 sequencing

Generation of Flp-In 293 lines with stable TBX5 expression (Lipofectamine 3000, pOG44 co-transfection, hygromycin selection ramped to 200 ug/mL); endogenous NKX2-5 and GATA4 expression confirmed by RNA-seq and Western blot

MPRA library assembly: 20 bp barcode addition by 24x PCR, Gibson cloning into SfiI-digested pGL4.23dXbadLuc, electroporation into 10-beta E. coli, maxi-prep, barcode-oligo association sequencing library construction, miniP+eGFP fragment insertion, RecBCD/AsiSI redigestion and giga-prep

MPRA transfection and RNA processing: five replicate transfections of Flp-In 293 cells, 48 h harvest, RNeasy extraction with on-column and Turbo DNase digests, biotinylated GFP-oligo hybridization capture, Superscript III cDNA synthesis, qPCR-normalized indexing PCR and NextSeq 2000 sequencing

headline.static_readiness: 0/14 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification); unexecuted, declared environment neither statically validated nor verified as the env that produced the results; n_exact_capture_unexecuted=0, n_fetch_required=4
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 3/14 (21%) of computational steps reach the stage-1 RI ceiling (C3, C4, C5 - the PrOBEX preprocessing, thresholding/enrichment and Poisson-fitting steps, where the authors' own public code, the Zenodo input data named in the README, and the pip pin ProBEX-snp==0.1.2 all coincide). The remaining 11 computational steps are NI. Two distinct causes: (i) the six MPRA/downstream steps (C9-C14) have no input-data axis at all - the paper deposits no MPRA or Bind-n-Seq raw sequencing data in any repository (GEO/SRA/ENA/dbGaP are never mentioned; the Data-and-code-availability section names code repositories only and states that libraries and cell lines are 'available upon request'); (ii) the externally-tooled steps (C1, C6, C7, C8, C14) run MEME, LS-GKM, MinSeqChIP, TOP LD and RELI with no version pin whatsoever. Capture claim is exact_pins_partial: PLINK(v1.90b) and HOMER (v5.1) in prose, ProBEX-snp==0.1.2 in the README, plus a conda-recipe/meta.yaml directory - but no lockfile, no container, no tagged release (the GitHub releases list is empty), and the MEME Suite is explicitly left to the user to download. Under rubric Delta-2 exact_pins_partial without environment closure caps version at 1, so even a perfect stage-2 code read yields no R-star gain: not a stage2 candidate on the positive gate.
headline.coverage: 14 computational steps and 5 wet-lab steps derived from the Materials and Methods prose of the bioRxiv JATS XML plus the PrOBEX README and the four cited repository landing pages. Wet-lab steps are OOS (not a computational reproduction target) and are excluded from S. No workflow source was read.

gaps.where: Data availability (paper 'Data and code availability' section) vs. all sequencing-derived steps C3-C14
gaps.missing: The paper deposits no sequencing data. The Data-and-code-availability section lists four code repositories and nothing else; Materials availability states only that 'The CHD libraries used for the SNP Bind-n-Seq and MPRA, and the genetically modified cell lines used in this work, are available upon request.' No GEO, SRA, ENA, ArrayExpress, dbGaP, EGA or figshare accession appears anywhere in the manuscript for the Bind-n-Seq PE150 reads, the MPRA barcode-association reads, or the MPRA cDNA/plasmid reads. The only sequencing identifiers cited are three third-party ChIP-seq experiments reused as model inputs (SRX9284027, SRX9284038, SRX2023721). Bind-n-Seq inputs are recoverable only because the PrOBEX README - not the paper - points to two Zenodo records (17907086 for NKX2-5/GATA4, 17910305 for TBX5); the MPRA raw data have no equivalent, so C9-C14 score data=0.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the Bind-n-Seq and MPRA FASTQ under a primary accession (GEO/SRA superseries) and cite it in the manuscript's Data availability section; add the two Zenodo DOIs to the paper itself rather than leaving them in the repository README; publish the MPRA count matrices and the emAllele/non-emAllele call tables as supplementary or archived files.

gaps.where: Software environment across all 14 computational steps (PrOBEX repo tree/README; Methods prose)
gaps.missing: No lockfile and no container. The PrOBEX repo tree carries setup.py, a conda-recipe/meta.yaml, MANIFEST.in and dist/, but no environment.yml with pinned builds, no requirements.txt with hashes, no conda-lock/pixi.lock, and no Dockerfile or image digest; the GitHub releases list is empty, so there is no tagged snapshot either. Prose pins cover only PLINK(v1.90b) and HOMER (v5.1); the README pins the authors' own package as ProBEX-snp==0.1.2. Python, scipy (used for the L-BFGS-B fit that produces the central K values), numpy, pandas, matplotlib and openpyxl versions are all unstated. The MEME Suite version is unstated and the README explicitly delegates its acquisition: 'MEME Suite: Must be downloaded and available in the working directory'. LS-GKM, MinSeqChIP, DESeq2, RELI, MPRAmatch and MPRAcount versions/commits are all unstated. OS closure is limited to 'Operating System: Linux (recommended)'; no BLAS/LAPACK statement, which matters for the numerical optimizer.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock or pixi.lock (or a Dockerfile plus published image digest) capturing Python, scipy and all transitive dependencies for a declared platform; pin the MEME Suite, LS-GKM, MinSeqChIP, DESeq2, RELI, MPRAmatch and MPRAcount to exact versions or commit SHAs; state the BLAS implementation used for the L-BFGS-B fitting.

gaps.where: Repository snapshots for all five cited code artifacts
gaps.missing: Every code link is a floating HEAD with no commit SHA, tag or archival DOI: github.com/Shreya-droid/SNPoiss_bind_n_seq (no releases; last push 2026-07-17, i.e. after the 2025-12 preprint, so HEAD is not the state described in the paper), github.com/tewhey-lab/MPRAmodel, github.com/WeirauchLab/mpraprofiler, github.com/WeirauchLab/RELI and github.com/tewhey-lab/MPRA_oligo_barcode_pipeline. Worse, the MPRAmatch URL cited verbatim in the Methods (https://github.com/tewhey-lab/MPRAmatch) returns HTTP 404 - the barcode-to-oligo association step of the MPRA arm currently has no reachable code at the address the paper gives.
gaps.how_to_close: Mint a tagged release of SNPoiss_bind_n_seq archived to Zenodo and cite the DOI plus commit SHA in the manuscript; cite exact commit SHAs for the four third-party pipelines; correct or replace the dead MPRAmatch URL.

gaps.where: Analysis parameters and seeds (Methods: 'Model training and testing', MEME/LS-GKM sections, Poisson fitting)
gaps.missing: Random seeds are never reported. The train/test construction explicitly randomizes ('These SNPs were randomly shuffled and subsequently divided into 300 SNPs for training and 200 SNPs for testing') and getNullSeqs negative-set generation is stochastic, so the reported model-comparison numbers are not reproducible without seeds. The Poisson fit's initial parameter guesses are described only as 'initial parameter guesses'; convergence tolerances for scipy L-BFGS-B and the bounds on the stuck-in-the-well parameter beyond [0,1] are unstated; the choice of denominators at iteration 361 out of 1000 is asserted from observed convergence rather than a stated criterion. LS-GKM is run in 'the default mode' without naming which defaults, and MEME's -maxw is rendered as 'maxw S' in the source text while the surrounding prose says 5-9 bases.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the random seeds for the shuffle, split and getNullSeqs calls; state optimizer tolerances, bounds and initialization; give an explicit convergence criterion for denominator selection; state the LS-GKM version and its effective default parameters.
